title: [YouPass Collect] - European transport fuel consumption comparison
prompt: The chart below shows information about fuel used in the transport sector in diﬀerent countries in Europe, compared to the EU average, in 2009 and 2010. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the percentage of fuel consumed in the transport sector across six European countries and the EU average in 2009 and 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the figures for Slovakia, Spain, and the EU average declined over the period, while those for Italy, France, and Greece recorded modest increases, and Austria remained unchanged. Slovakia consistently recorded the highest fuel usage in both years by a considerable margin, whereas Greece reported the lowest throughout.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Turning to the countries with falling figures, Slovakia stood out as the heaviest fuel consumer in 2009, at 8.8%, which was well above the EU average of 6% and more than double Spain's figure of 3.8%. By 2010, Slovakia's proportion had dropped noticeably to 6.5%, while Spain's figure also declined, albeit more modestly, to 3%. Similarly, the EU average fell from 6% to 5% over the same period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In contrast, the remaining countries all saw their figures either rise or hold steady between the two years. In 2009, Austria recorded 5.2%, somewhat above Italy's 4.5% and considerably higher than France's 3.7% and Greece's mere 1.2%. Austria's proportion remained unchanged in 2010, while Italy and France both experienced slight increases, reaching 5.2% and 4.3%, respectively. Greece, despite having the lowest starting point, saw the most significant relative growth among all countries, with its figure rising by approximately two-thirds, from 1.2% to 2%.
